protocolIssues.rootCause: WordPress Address (site_url) configuration in wp_options is set to "http://firstread.co.uk" (HTTP) while Site Address (home) is "https://firstread.co.uk" (HTTPS).
protocolIssues.recommendation: Update WordPress Address (URL) in WordPress General Settings (or define WP_SITEURL in wp-config.php) to "https://firstread.co.uk". This ensures plugins and REST API links do not generate HTTP URLs.
protocolIssues.details: WordPress site_url is configured as "http://firstread.co.uk" (HTTP) while home is "https://firstread.co.uk" (HTTPS). All HTTP requests 301-redirect to HTTPS, but configuration inconsistency causes downstream plugins to output HTTP URLs.

protocolIssues.rootCause: Yoast SEO inherits the HTTP WordPress Address (site_url) setting when writing the robots.txt Sitemap directive.
protocolIssues.recommendation: Fixing WordPress Address to HTTPS in WordPress settings will automatically update robots.txt to output the HTTPS sitemap URL.
protocolIssues.details: Robots.txt declares an HTTP sitemap directive: "http://firstread.co.uk/sitemap_index.xml". Crawlers will follow the 301 redirect to HTTPS, but best practice is declaring direct HTTPS to conserve crawl budget.

protocolIssues.recommendation: Updating WordPress Address to HTTPS will cause Yoast to output HTTPS sub-sitemaps automatically.

rootCauseGroups.description: WordPress site_url in wp_options is set to "http://firstread.co.uk" while home is "https://firstread.co.uk".
